India was described as a strong growth engine, but no figures were given in these pages.

rd.auditor: Auditor (FY2025-26): opinion unmodified; emphasis of matter: Insurance claim recoverability at subsidiary Daawat Foods, ₹13,410.53 lakh, pending High Court appeal (consolidated); key audit matters: 1; contingent liabilities: not disclosed.

story.what_it_does: LT Foods sells basmati and specialty rice (its largest business, ₹9,742 crore of ₹11,023 crore FY26 revenue), plus organic foods and ingredients and ready-to-heat products. North America made up 48% of FY26 revenue, with India, Europe and the UK also important.
story.plans: Management targets a ₹100 million pound UK revenue goal, a 13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin over the long term, and ready-to-heat breakeven at about ₹400 crore revenue. It also wants organic EBITDA margin back to 7% by end FY27 and ROCE up to 23%, with capex around ₹250 crore a year.
story.moat: The notes point to brand strength (Daawat and others), with India market share of 22.3% to 23.1% and basmati EBITDA margin of 13% in Q1 FY27. The notes do not describe other moat sources explicitly, and market share slipped over the period.

scenarios.story: Basmati growth stays strong (34% in Q1 FY27, with volume up 11%) and leverage stays low (net cash ₹247 crore). Organic and ready-to-heat fixes then lift margins toward management's 13.5% goal.
signals_to_watch: Organic business EBITDA margin moving from 4% toward the 7% year-end target
Ready-to-heat capacity becoming operational as promised and revenue scaling toward ₹300 crore

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps growing but more slowly (17% in Q2 FY27, versus 26% in Q1), with EBITDA margin around 11% as brand spend and freight weigh. Profit grows about 10% a year in the recent quarters.
signals_to_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin staying near 11% to 11.5% versus the 13.5% target
Advertising spend near the guided 2.3% of sales for FY27

scenarios.story: Tariffs, duties and freight costs keep squeezing margins, and the headline growth proves to be partly one-off, since normalised growth was much lower earlier. Gross margin has already slid to 32.5% and Europe, the UK and organic remain challenged.
signals_to_watch: Gross margin falling further below 32.5%, or no clear outcome on US tariff refunds and the CVD appeal
India market share slipping further below 22.3% or a poor rice crop from El Nino
